A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research framework, renamed from CTRA to CPRA. Their complete text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial reorganization and formatting changes.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendix D report original MIS, MaxCut, and diverse bipartite matching experiments, including runtimes, approximation rates, and solution diversity.

after.justification: Section 6 and Appendix D retain those empirical results. Appendix E additionally reports an original comparison of two-stage and scratch training on weighted MIS tasks.

M1.justification: Section 5.1 and Appendix E introduce a two-stage extension: train on a task subset, freeze the encoder, replace the output head, and train that head on the full task set. The core shared GNN, parallel relaxation, and diversity objective remain unchanged under the CPRA name.

E1.justification: Appendix E adds 500 weighted MIS tasks on a fixed 1,000-node, degree-5 regular graph, extending the earlier unweighted MIS coverage to varying node-weight objectives. The existing MIS, Gset MaxCut, and CORA-derived matching coverage is retained.

E2.justification: New Table 3 introduces Scratch-500, a scratch-trained 500-head model, as the explicit comparator for the two-stage extension. Comparator membership in the retained PI-GNN, CRA, greedy, and RUN-CSP comparisons remains unchanged.

E3.justification: Appendix E adds a protocol using 200 warm-up tasks for up to 8,000 epochs, followed by 2,000 epochs of head training across 500 tasks, with distinct annealing schedules and a 10^-4 entropy stopping threshold. It reports average weight and stage-specific runtime; existing benchmark settings are otherwise retained.

E4.justification: Appendix E adds a comparison testing the combined warm-up and frozen-encoder strategy against scratch training for runtime and solution quality. Existing analyses of shot-count scaling, diversity strength, Hamming distances, PCA distributions, and exploration across Gset instances are retained.

E5.justification: v2 Section 5.1 explicitly states that all MIS results summarize five RRGs with different seeds; v3 omits this statement. Five-seed standard-deviation descriptions elsewhere remain, so this is a loss of reporting specificity without evidence that run counts changed.

E6.justification: New Table 3 reports 73.9 seconds and average weight 139.87 for two-stage training, versus 83.7 seconds and 123.87 for Scratch-500. These are additional weighted-task results. Numerical entries in the retained main comparison tables, Gset Table 2, and multi-instance DBM results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: v3 corrects the background entropy exponent condition from odd values {2n-1} to even values {2n}, restricts the penalty-weight domain, and removes the cross-entropy alternative. Both versions already use alpha = 2 experimentally. The central convergence theorem, Hamming–variance identity, and appendix proofs retain their substance.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the central claims: obtaining penalty- and variation-diversified solutions within one training run, sharing representations with approximately single-solution model size and runtime, and improving exploration and solution quality. Renaming and expanded emphasis do not materially redefine these claims.

C2.justification: Section 2 newly interprets penalty diversification through Pareto trade-offs and explicitly identifies broader neural-method and Pareto comparisons as outside scope or future work. Appendix E attributes its new findings to encoder reuse. The earlier discussion of cross-entropy's endpoint-gradient difficulties is removed.

D1.justification: v3 adds a code-availability link on page 1 and documents the extension's training schedules, encoder freezing, head replacement, and stopping threshold. Existing GNN architecture, AdamW settings, V100 hardware, and rounding details are retained.

R1.justification: The rewritten related-work section substantially broadens positioning beyond classical diverse-solution algorithms to neural diversity methods and multiobjective/Pareto learning, including POMO, PolyNet, and works by Navon et al. and Lin et al. It explains differences in objectives and comparison scope; several earlier citations, including Deb, Sun et al., and Sanokowski et al., are removed.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, and method explanations undergo extensive rewriting. Related work moves before the background, notation becomes a separate section, and background and method material gains numbered subsections. The title, method terminology, author information, and publication headers also change.

P2.justification: The document adopts a different journal layout with changed typography, text area, and figure sizing and placement. Figure 1 expands from an inset to a full-width display, existing plots are restyled and enlarged, Table 1 moves into Appendix C.3, and Table 3 is added.

improvement.justification: Clearer research positioning, a new code link, and Appendix E's comparison with scratch training add useful context and evidence for the extension while preserving the existing empirical results. The gains are limited by unspecified repetitions, uncertainty, and scratch-training budget in the new study, together with the loss of the explicit five-RRG aggregation statement.
